scope: Proposition 5.19 (Conditional projection rule) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 75-76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 ≤ S ≤ 2, 0 < b ≤ 1, and ∆ ↓ 0. Let Z be a bounded planar source, W a record determining a direction g(W), and D common side data. Assume I(Z; W | D) = o(log(1/∆)). (5.5) Suppose there is an event G of probability bounded below such that its unnormalized conditional marginals obey, for every needed ball and interval of radius ∆ ≤ r ≤ 1, P(G, Z ∈ B(z, r) | D) ≤ ∆−o(1) rS , P(G, g(W) ∈ J(r) | D) ≤ ∆−o(1) rb . (5.6) 75 For each D, W, let I(D, W) be a list of at most ∆−x−o(1) intervals of length O(∆), and suppose that on G the projection of Z in direction g(W) belongs to their union, up to O(∆) error. Then x ≥ min{S, (S + b)/2, 1}. (5.7) The assertion is a strict-error statement: a fixed strict deficit is impossible if all preceding exponent losses and the information ratio are sufficiently small. Consequently a sufficiently fine finite grid of prefix radii suffices, and errors of size ∆1−o(1) in directions, representatives, or output resolution are allowed. The same conclusion holds with c∆ = P(G) tending to zero, provided log(1/c∆) = o(log(1/∆)), I(Z; W | D) = o(c∆ log(1/∆)).
